newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN chief wants meeting on Afghanistan Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: UN chief wants meeting on Afghanistan Nov 18.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali has called a meeting for Nov. 18 on how to promote national reconcialition among warring parties in Afghanistan, U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa said on Wednesday.
The meeting, she said, would "enable the United Nations to present a detailed account of the action it is taking" and to ask for support from member states.
Boutros-Ghali will chair the session at U.N. headquarters in New York, and Norbert Holl of Germany, the special U.N representative for Afghanistan, will attend, she said.
Foa said none of the Afghan parties, neither the Taleban nor the country's ousted government, would attend the meeting.

Those invited were foreign ministers or their represenatives from China, France, Germany, India, Iran, Italy, Japan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Tajikistan, Turkey, Turmenistan, Uzbekistan, Britain and the United States.
Iran has recently called for such a conference, but the idea was greeted coolly by the United States.
